mainTopic: Coins, חליפין, and symbolic acquisition: "sell me for these," exchanges with set prices, whose vessel is used, and whether produce can be used.
overview: The amud opens by finishing a ruling: if a buyer says "sell me for these" and the seller doesn't care about the exact sum, the buyer acquires at once, like חליפין, but there is still אונאה. In רב אבא's report, רב הונא says there is no אונאה. The גמרא then asks about a real חליפין where the parties do care about the values. A ברייתא about trading a cow for a donkey seems to show such a trade fails, but רבא explains that the ברייתא is about an incomplete משיכה. Next the גמרא asks whether רב הונא lets a coin act as חליפין, and another version has him say plainly that it cannot. רב and לוי then argue whose vessel is used for symbolic חליפין, and the גמרא ties this to a dispute of תנאים about the shoe in רות. רב נחמן and רב ששת argue whether produce can be used, each reading the same פסוק. The amud ends with the wording of documents, whose explanation continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The ruling ends: there is still a claim of overcharging
steps.stepSummary: The earlier ruling ends by saying that the seller can still claim אונאה against the buyer.
steps.simpleTranslation: And he has a claim of overcharging against him.
steps.whatsHappening: These are the last words of a ruling that started before this section. The buyer gave coins without the seller caring about the exact amount. The ruling adds that the seller can still make a claim of אונאה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The full ruling has two parts: the buyer acquires, and there is still אונאה. This line is the second part. The next step explains both parts.

keyTerms.meaning: Overcharging or underpaying by a sixth or more of the item's value. The cheated side can claim the difference.
He has a claim against him

phrases.english: And he has a claim of overcharging against him.
phrases.notes: Here the seller is the one who can claim. The coins were worth less than the item.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends a ruling that began before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In the coins-without-caring case, the seller can claim אונאה.

steps.title: Explaining both parts of the ruling
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains two things. The buyer acquires without משיכה because the seller didn't care, which makes it like חליפין. There is still אונאה because the buyer used the words "sell me."
steps.simpleTranslation: He acquires even though he did not pull the item. Since the seller was not particular, the buyer acquires, because it is like an exchange. And there is still a claim of overcharging, because the buyer said to him: "Sell me for these."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains each half of the ruling. It says why the buyer owns the item right away, and why a claim of אונאה still applies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually coins do not finalize a purchase of movable items; you need משיכה. But here the seller didn't care how much he got, so the coins act like an object traded in חליפין, and that finalizes the deal at once. Still, the buyer used the word "sell," so it counts as a sale, and sales carry the rules of אונאה.

keyTerms.meaning: Pulled. Refers to מְשִׁיכָה, pulling the item to acquire it.
Is particular, cares exactly about the amount
Exchange or barter. It finalizes a deal at once.

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the deal stops being a sale. It works LIKE חליפין for acquiring, but the words "sell me" keep it a sale for the laws of אונאה.

phrases.aramaic: קָנָה – אַף עַל גַּב דְּלָא מָשַׁךְ,
phrases.english: He acquires – even though he did not pull it,
because since he is not particular – he acquires,
phrases.notes: "He" who isn't particular is the seller. He doesn't care about the exact sum of coins.

phrases.english: as it is similar to an exchange.
And he has a claim of overcharging against him –
because he said to him: "Sell me for these."

steps.triggerLanguage: קָנָה – אַף עַל גַּב דְּלָא מָשַׁךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reason behind the ruling just completed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Coins the seller doesn't care about work like חליפין to finalize the deal. But the words "sell me" keep אונאה in force.

steps.title: Another report of רב הונא: no claim of overcharging
steps.stepSummary: רב אבא quotes רב הונא: with "sell me for these," the buyer acquires and there is NO אונאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אבא said in the name of רב הונא: if he said "Sell me for these," the buyer acquires, and there is no claim of overcharging.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אבא reports רב הונא's ruling differently. This version agrees that the buyer acquires, but it says there is no אונאה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both versions of רב הונא's ruling agree the deal is final right away. They differ on whether the word "sell" makes this a sale. In this version, רב הונא treats the whole deal as true חליפין, and חליפין has no אונאה.

keyTerms.meaning: And he does not have [a claim]

steps.whatToRemember: Two reports of רב הונא: (1) acquires + אונאה; (2) רב אבא's report: acquires + no אונאה.

phrases.english: Rav Abba said that Rav Huna said:
"Sell me for these" – he acquires,
and he has no claim of overcharging against him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different report of the same ruling of רב הונא, differing on the אונאה half.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: With "sell me for these," the deal is final and there is no אונאה.

steps.title: The reverse question: an exchange where values matter
steps.stepSummary: The first case is clear: money not counted carefully works like חליפין. But what about a real חליפין where the parties do care about the values?
steps.simpleTranslation: It is obvious that with money the seller isn't particular about, we already said the buyer acquires, since it is like an exchange. But an exchange where they are particular about the values, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets aside the case it already solved. It asks a new question: if two people trade items but care about the values, is that treated as a sale or as an exchange?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier case made money act like חליפין, because nobody cared about the amount. Now the reverse: real items are traded, but the parties put prices on them. Maybe caring about the prices turns the trade into a sale, which would need משיכה.

keyTerms.meaning: Particular about them, cares about their exact value

phrases.english: It is obvious: money, and he is not particular about it –
we already said that he acquires,
as it is like an exchange.
An exchange, and he is particular about them – what?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on step 2's idea and turns it around.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is a trade of items with exact prices a חליפין, which finalizes at once, or a sale?

steps.title: A proof begins: the cow-and-donkey case
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא בר אהבה starts quoting a ברייתא. A man stands with his cow. Another man offers him a donkey, and each says a price for his own animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אדא בר אהבה said: Come and hear. A man was holding his cow and standing there. Another came and asked, "Why your cow?" He answered, "I need a donkey." "I have a donkey I can give you. How much is your cow?" "So much." "How much is your donkey?" "So much."
steps.whatsHappening: רב אדא בר אהבה brings a ברייתא to answer the question. This is only the setup: the story's case is being laid out, and its ruling comes later.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא fits the question exactly. The two men are trading animals, which is חליפין. But they put a price on each animal, so they care about the values. Whatever the ברייתא rules will show how such a trade is treated.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה, תָּא שְׁמַע:
phrases.english: Rav Adda bar Ahava said: Come and hear:
There was one who was holding his cow and standing,
and another came and said to him:
Why your cow?
phrases.notes: He means: why are you standing here with your cow?

phrases.english: I need a donkey.

phrases.aramaic: יֵשׁ לִי חֲמוֹר שֶׁאֲנִי נוֹתֵן לְךָ.
phrases.english: I have a donkey that I can give you.
Your cow, for how much? For such-and-such.
Your donkey, for how much? For such-and-such.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה, תָּא שְׁמַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts answering step 4's question with a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: Whether a trade with exact prices counts as חליפין or as a sale
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about trading a cow for a donkey, with a price set for each. Its ruling comes in the next step.

steps.title: The ending of the cow-and-donkey ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא ends: the donkey's owner pulled the cow, the donkey died before the cow's owner pulled it, and the donkey's owner did not acquire the cow.
steps.simpleTranslation: The owner of the donkey pulled the cow. The owner of the cow did not manage to pull the donkey before the donkey died. So the owner of the donkey did not acquire the cow.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting the ברייתא that רב אדא בר אהבה started. This is the ruling the גמרא wants to use to answer its question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In a normal חליפין, once one side pulls his new item, the whole trade is done. Then the other side owns his new item too, wherever it is. Here one side pulled, yet the ברייתא says the trade did not happen, so the ברייתא seems to break the normal rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Pulled. This is the act of משיכה, which makes a purchase take effect for movable items.

phrases.english: The owner of the donkey pulled the cow,
but the owner of the cow did not manage
to pull the donkey
before the donkey died,

phrases.aramaic: לֹא קָנָה בַּעַל הַחֲמוֹר אֶת הַפָּרָה.
phrases.english: the owner of the donkey did not acquire the cow.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא that Step 5 began quoting.
steps.raayaObject: Whether a חליפין where both sides valued their items takes effect when only one side pulls.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of the cow and the donkey, where each owner stated a price.

steps.title: Lesson from the ברייתא: a carefully valued trade does not take effect
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes from the ברייתא that a חליפין where the sides care about the values does not take effect on one pull.
steps.simpleTranslation: Learn from this: in a trade where the sides care about the values, the buyer does not acquire.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא uses the ברייתא to answer the question from Step 4. A חליפין where the sides care about the values does not work the usual way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the ברייתא each owner named a price for his animal, so they clearly cared about the values. Since the ברייתא says there was no acquisition, the גמרא infers that this kind of careful trade is not finished until both sides pull.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from this. Introduces a conclusion drawn from a source.
Acquiring by exchange: when one side takes his item, the other side acquires the other item.
Particular, careful about the exact values.

phrases.english: Learn from this:
an exchange where he is particular about them,
phrases.notes: "Them" means the values of the items being traded, like the prices each owner named in the ברייתא.

phrases.english: he does not acquire.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a rule from the ruling of the ברייתא in Step 6.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a real חליפין where the sides care about the values takes effect on one pull (Step 4).
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: No. When the sides are particular about the values, one pull is not enough.

steps.title: רבא: everyone cares about value in a trade
steps.stepSummary: רבא rejects the inference, because all people who trade care about the values, and חליפין still works for them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Do you think that in חליפין we are dealing with fools who don't care about the values? Rather, in every חליפין the sides certainly care, and still the buyer acquires.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא pushes back on the lesson from Step 7. Caring about the values cannot be what stopped the acquisition, because everyone who trades cares about the values.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If caring about the values cancelled חליפין, then חליפין would only work for fools who don't check what they get, which makes no sense. So רבא says normal חליפין always involves caring, and it still takes effect on one pull. That means the ברייתא needs a different explanation, which comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that to say? Introduces a question that rejects an idea.

steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not saying the ברייתא is wrong. He agrees there was no acquisition there; he only rejects the reason Step 7 gave for it.

phrases.english: Rava said:
Is that to say that with exchange we are dealing with fools,
who are not particular?
Rather, in every exchange
they are certainly particular, and he acquires.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: אַטּוּ חֲלִיפִין בְּשׁוּפְטָנֵי עָסְקִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the inference drawn in Step 7.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The idea that caring about the values stops חליפין from working.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: People always care about values when trading, so the inference would leave חליפין only for fools.

steps.title: רבא's reading: donkey for a cow plus a lamb
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains the ברייתא as a trade of a donkey for a cow and a lamb, where only the cow was pulled, so the משיכה was incomplete.
steps.simpleTranslation: So what case is the ברייתא talking about? One said to the other: a donkey for a cow and a lamb. He pulled the cow but had not yet pulled the lamb, so his pulling was not a complete pulling.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a new explanation of why the ברייתא says there was no acquisition. The donkey's owner was supposed to receive two animals and pulled only one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The deal was the donkey in exchange for both a cow and a lamb. Pulling just the cow is only half the משיכה, so the trade never closed. The donkey therefore still belonged to its original owner when it died. Now the ברייתא fits without saying that careful trades fail.

keyTerms.meaning: With what case are we dealing? Introduces a narrower way to read a source.

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבא, normal חליפין takes effect even when the sides care about the values. The ברייתא failed only because the משיכה was incomplete: the cow was pulled, but not the lamb.
steps.whyThisMatters: This keeps the basic rule of חליפין in place: one side taking his item completes the deal, as long as he took everything he was getting.

phrases.english: And here, with what are we dealing?
Where he said to him:
a donkey for a cow and a lamb,
and he pulled the cow
and had not yet pulled the lamb,
so it was not a proper pulling for him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes רבא's rejection by giving a new reading of the ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Recasting the case (אוקימתא): the ברייתא is about a trade of one item for two items.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The trade failed because the sides cared about the values.
steps.terutzMaskana: The trade failed because only part of the משיכה was done: the cow was pulled, but not the lamb.

steps.title: Does רב הונא hold that a coin can be used for חליפין?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא repeats רב הונא's ruling about 'sell me for these' and suggests that it means a coin can work as the item of a חליפין.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: 'Sell me for these': he acquires, and the seller has a claim of אונאה against him. Shall we say that רב הונא holds that a coin can be used for חליפין?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to רב הונא's ruling and quotes it again so it can ask a new question about it. This sets up a discussion of what רב הונא really holds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רב הונא's case the buyer acquires right away just by handing over coins, without משיכה, which looks like חליפין. That suggests רב הונא lets a coin serve as the exchange item. The גמרא raises this with לימא, a suggestion it will now test.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say? Introduces a suggestion the גמרא will test.
Overcharging or underpaying by too much, which gives the cheated side a claim.

phrases.english: The Master said:
phrases.notes: "The Master" here is רב הונא, whose ruling the גמרא is repeating.

phrases.english: "Sell me for these": he acquires,
and he has a claim of exploitation against him.
Shall we say that Rav Huna holds
that a coin can be used for exchange?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר: מְכוֹר לִי בְּאֵלּוּ – קָנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the ברייתא and goes back to רב הונא's ruling to ask a new question about it.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רב הונא's ruling means he holds that a coin can be used for חליפין.

steps.title: רב הונא's ruling is really about money acquiring by Torah law
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the idea that רב הונא lets a coin act as חליפין. He holds like רבי יוחנן that money acquires by Torah law, and the rabbinic decree requiring משיכה only covers common cases.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. רב הונא holds like רבי יוחנן, who said that by Torah law money acquires. Why did the Sages say that pulling acquires? It is a decree, so the seller won't say 'your wheat burned in the attic.' The Sages made decrees only for common situations, not for uncommon ones.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the suggestion from step 10. It says רב הונא's case is not חליפין at all. Instead, it is a normal sale with money, which works by Torah law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי יוחנן, paying money is enough by Torah law. The Sages required משיכה only to stop a seller from being careless with goods that were already paid for. That decree covers everyday situations, and רב הונא's case is unusual, so the Torah law stays in place and the money acquires.

keyTerms.meaning: By Torah law, as opposed to rabbinic law
Money acquires, meaning payment completes the sale
A rabbinic decree made as a safeguard
An upper story or attic where goods were stored

steps.confusionAlert: The coin here is not being used as a חליפין item. It is acting as ordinary payment, which acquires by Torah law.
steps.whyThisMatters: This removes the proof that a coin can be חליפין. The next step gives a version where רב הונא states his view directly.

phrases.english: No, Rav Huna holds
like Rabbi Yochanan, who said:
By Torah law, money acquires.
And why did they say that pulling acquires?
It is a decree, in case the seller says to him:
'Your wheat was burned in the attic.'
For a common situation, the Sages made a decree,

phrases.aramaic: וּמִלְּתָא דְּלָא שְׁכִיחָא – לָא גְּזַרוּ בַּהּ רַבָּנַן.
phrases.english: but for an uncommon situation, the Sages did not make a decree.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא, רַב הוּנָא סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the inference drawn in step 10 from רב הונא's ruling.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof that a coin can serve as חליפין
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רב הונא's case can be explained as money acquiring by Torah law, with no rabbinic decree for an uncommon case. It does not need to be חליפין.

steps.title: Another version: רב הונא explicitly says a coin cannot be חליפין
steps.stepSummary: מר הונא בריה דרב נחמן tells רב אשי that in his yeshiva, רב הונא's ruling is taught directly: a coin cannot become חליפין.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר הונא, son of רב נחמן, said to רב אשי: You teach it that way, but we teach it this way: 'And likewise רב הונא said: a coin cannot become חליפין.'
steps.whatsHappening: A different version of רב הונא's teaching is reported. In this version, there is no inference to argue about, because he states the rule directly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier discussion tried to learn רב הונא's view from his case, and step 11 only rejected that inference. In this version, רב הונא plainly says a coin cannot be used as the item of חליפין, so there is nothing left to infer.

keyTerms.meaning: 'You teach' and 'we teach'; this introduces a different version of a teaching
Becomes the item that effects a חליפין exchange

steps.whatToRemember: The bottom line: a coin cannot be used as the item of חליפין.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ מָר הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב נַחְמָן לְרַב אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: Mar Huna, son of Rav Nachman, said to Rav Ashi:
You teach it this way,
we teach it this way:
And likewise Rav Huna said,
a coin cannot become a חליפין.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַתּוּן, הָכִי מַתְנִיתוּ לַהּ, אֲנַן הָכִי מַתְנֵינַן לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an alternate version of רב הונא's teaching that avoids the inference debated in steps 10-11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A coin cannot serve as the item of חליפין.

steps.title: Whose vessel is used for a symbolic exchange?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which vessel is used in a symbolic חליפין: the buyer's or the seller's.
steps.simpleTranslation: With what does one acquire?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic and asks a short question. The next steps give the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In a symbolic חליפין, an object such as a cloth is handed over to make a sale take effect. The question is whose object it has to be: the person acquiring or the person transferring ownership.

phrases.english: With what does one acquire?
phrases.notes: He is asking whose vessel or cloth is used to make a symbolic exchange take effect.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic about symbolic חליפין.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the vessel used in a symbolic חליפין belongs to the buyer or to the seller.

steps.title: רב: the buyer's vessel is used
steps.stepSummary: רב says the exchange is done with the vessel of the one acquiring. The buyer is glad to let the seller acquire his vessel so that the seller will commit to the deal.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: with the vessel of the buyer. The buyer is happy to let the seller acquire his vessel, so that the seller will make up his mind and transfer ownership to him.
steps.whatsHappening: רב answers the question. The buyer gives his own vessel to the seller, and that completes the deal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב explains why this makes sense. The buyer wants the land or item, so he is willing to give up his vessel to get the seller to finalize the sale.

keyTerms.meaning: A vessel or object used for the symbolic exchange
The one transferring ownership, the seller
So that he resolves or commits

phrases.english: Rav said: with the vessel of the one acquiring.
For the one acquiring is pleased
to have the one transferring ownership acquire his vessel,
so that he will commit and transfer ownership to him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives רב's answer to the question of step 13.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The buyer's vessel is used, given to the seller.

steps.title: לוי: the seller's vessel is used
steps.stepSummary: לוי says the exchange is done with the seller's vessel, and the reason will be explained later.
steps.simpleTranslation: And לוי said: with the vessel of the seller, as we will explain later.
steps.whatsHappening: לוי gives the opposite answer: the seller's vessel is used. The גמרא promises to explain his reason further on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By לוי's view, the buyer takes hold of the seller's object, and through that he acquires the item being sold. This sets up the challenge in the next step.

phrases.english: And Levi said: with the vessel of the one transferring ownership,
as we will explain below.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing answer to רב's.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The seller's vessel is used, taken by the buyer.

steps.title: Challenge to לוי: land would be acquired along with a cloak
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא מדסקרתא challenges לוי. If the buyer takes the seller's cloak, then land is being acquired along with movable property, but the משנה teaches the opposite.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא מדסקרתא said to רבא: According to לוי, who says the seller's vessel is used, one acquires land along with a cloak. If so, guaranteed property (land) is acquired along with non-guaranteed property (movables). But we learned the reverse: non-guaranteed property is acquired along with guaranteed property!
steps.whatsHappening: A question is raised against לוי's view. It seems to flip a rule from a משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says movables can be acquired 'along with' land, so land is the main item and movables ride along with it. In לוי's view the buyer takes the cloak, and through that he gets the land. That makes the land ride along with the cloak, which is backwards.

keyTerms.meaning: Along with, by means of; one item is acquired through another
Property with a guarantee, meaning land
Property without a guarantee, meaning movables

steps.confusionAlert: 'Property with אחריות' means land, not just any valuable item.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב הוּנָא מִדִּסְקַרְתָּא לְרָבָא:
phrases.english: Rav Huna from Diskarta said to Rava:
But according to Levi, who said with the vessel of the one transferring ownership,

phrases.aramaic: הָא קָא קָנֵי אַרְעָא אַגַּב גְּלִימָא.
phrases.english: then he is acquiring land along with a cloak.
If so, it turns out to be
property that has a guarantee
phrases.notes: That's land, which a lender can collect from even after it's sold. Movables can't be collected that way.

phrases.aramaic: וְנִקְנִין עִם נְכָסִים שֶׁאֵין לָהֶן אַחְרָיוּת.
phrases.english: being acquired along with property that has no guarantee.
But we learned the reverse:
phrases.notes: This is the משנה in קידושין 26a.

phrases.english: Property that has no guarantee

phrases.aramaic: נִקְנִין עִם נְכָסִים שֶׁיֵּשׁ לָהֶן אַחְרָיוּת!
phrases.english: is acquired along with property that has a guarantee!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks לוי's opinion from step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: לוי's view that the seller's vessel is used
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Under לוי, land is acquired through the cloak. That reverses the משנה's rule that movables are acquired along with land, not land along with movables.

steps.title: The land is transferred because of the seller's pleasure, not along with the cloak
steps.stepSummary: The challenge is rejected. The seller does not transfer the land together with the cloak. Instead, he is pleased that the buyer accepted his cloak, and in return he decides to transfer the land.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: If לוי were here, he would whip you with rods of fire! Do you think the land is transferred together with the cloak? No. Because of the pleasure the seller gets when the buyer accepts the cloak from him, the seller makes up his mind and transfers the land to him.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא defends לוי against the challenge from Step 16 and explains how his opinion really works.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge assumed that under לוי the land and the cloak change hands at the same moment, like 'land acquired along with movables.' The answer says no: the cloak is not part of the deal at all. The seller's satisfaction at having his cloak accepted is the 'payment' that makes him willing to transfer the land.

keyTerms.meaning: Rods of fire, a sharp way of saying 'you would be punished for that question.'
A cloak, the item used for the exchange.
He makes up his mind and transfers ownership.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אִי הֲוָה לֵוִי הָכָא,
phrases.english: He said to him: If לוי were here,
he would bring out rods of fire before you!
phrases.notes: A strong way of saying it: your question gets לוי so wrong that you'd deserve to be punished.

phrases.english: Do you think he transfers the land to him through the cloak itself?
Rather, because of that pleasure, that the buyer accepts the cloak from him,
he makes up his mind and transfers the land to him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 16.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reframes the mechanism: the land is not transferred together with the cloak.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Under לוי, the land and the cloak change hands at the same moment, so this would be land acquired along with movables.
steps.terutzMaskana: The seller's pleasure at having his cloak accepted moves him to transfer the land. There is no simultaneous transfer.

steps.title: The dispute matches a dispute of תנאים; the verse in רות is explained
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says the רב–לוי dispute matches a dispute of תנאים. It quotes the verse in רות about the shoe and explains that 'redemption' means a sale and 'exchange' means חליפין.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is like a dispute of תנאים. The verse says: 'This was the custom in earlier times in Israel concerning redemption and concerning exchange, to confirm every matter: a man drew off his shoe and gave it to his fellow.' 'Redemption' means a sale, as another verse says 'it shall not be redeemed.' 'Exchange' means חליפין, as another verse says 'he shall not exchange it nor substitute it.'
steps.whatsHappening: This step sets up the next move. The גמרא announces a parallel dispute among תנאים and first lays out the verse it is built on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before showing the dispute itself, the ברייתא shows that this verse is a source for חליפין. The word 'תמורה' in the verse is tied to the same word used for exchanging a קרבן. So the shoe ceremony in רות is a real act of acquiring through exchange.

keyTerms.meaning: This matches a dispute among the תנאים.

phrases.english: This is like a dispute of תנאים:
"Now this was the custom in former times in Israel
concerning redemption and concerning exchange,
to confirm every matter:
a man drew off his shoe and gave it to his fellow."
"Redemption" means a sale,
and so it says: "It shall not be redeemed."
"Exchange" means חליפין,

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵן הוּא אוֹמֵר: ״לֹא יַחֲלִיפֶנּוּ וְלֹא יָמִיר אוֹתוֹ״.
phrases.english: and so it says: "He shall not exchange it nor substitute it."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from defending לוי to showing that the whole רב–לוי dispute already exists among תנאים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The verse in רות about the shoe is a source for sale and for חליפין.

steps.title: Who gave the shoe to whom?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks who handed the shoe to whom in the story of רות.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'To confirm every matter: a man drew off his shoe and gave it to his fellow.' Who gave to whom?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא asks a question about the verse, setting up the dispute in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse does not say who took off the shoe: the one acquiring the field (בועז) or the one giving up his right (the גואל). That missing detail is exactly the question of whose item is used for חליפין.

keyTerms.meaning: His fellow, the other side of the deal.

phrases.english: "To confirm every matter:
a man drew off his shoe and gave it to his fellow."
Who gave to whom?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks the key question about the verse just quoted.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the shoe was given by the acquirer or by the one transferring the right.

steps.title: בועז gave to the גואל; רבי יהודה says the גואל gave to בועז
steps.stepSummary: The תנא קמא says בועז, the one acquiring, gave his shoe. This matches רב. רבי יהודה says the גואל, the one transferring, gave his shoe. This matches לוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: בועז gave to the redeemer. רבי יהודה says: The redeemer gave to בועז.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives two answers, and these are the two sides that match רב and לוי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בועז was the one acquiring the field. If he gave his shoe, the acquirer's item is used, like רב. If the גואל gave his shoe, the transferring side's item is used, like לוי.

keyTerms.meaning: The one acquiring the right to the field.
The closer relative, who gave up his right to the field.

steps.whatToRemember: תנא קמא (בועז gave) = רב (the acquirer's vessel). רבי יהודה (the גואל gave) = לוי (the seller's vessel).
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the roles. בועז is the buyer here, and the גואל is the one giving up the field.

phrases.english: בועז gave to the redeemer.
phrases.notes: The 'redeemer' is the closer relative who gave up his right to the field to בועז.

phrases.english: רבי יהודה says:
The redeemer gave to בועז.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 19.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The תנא קמא says the acquirer gave his shoe, like רב. רבי יהודה says the transferring side gave his shoe, like לוי.

steps.title: A vessel works for חליפין even if worth less than a פרוטה
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that one can acquire through a vessel even if the vessel is worth less than a פרוטה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: One may acquire with a vessel even if it is not worth a פרוטה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic: what kind of item can be used for symbolic חליפין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since this kind of חליפין is symbolic and not real payment, the item's value does not matter. Even a vessel worth less than a פרוטה works.

keyTerms.meaning: Worth a פרוטה, the smallest amount that counts as value.

phrases.english: It was taught: One may acquire with a vessel

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ שָׁוֶה פְּרוּטָה.
phrases.english: even though it is not worth a פרוטה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic about which items work for חליפין.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A vessel works for חליפין regardless of its value.

steps.title: רב נחמן: only a vessel; רב ששת: even produce
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן limits the ברייתא to vessels and excludes produce. רב ששת says even produce works.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: They taught this only with a vessel, but not with produce. רב ששת said: Even with produce.
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים argue about whether the ברייתא's rule applies only to vessels or also to produce.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן reads the word 'vessel' in the ברייתא as a limit. רב ששת holds that any item, even produce, can be used for symbolic חליפין.

keyTerms.meaning: They taught this only in the case of...
Produce, here meaning items that are not vessels.

phrases.english: רב נחמן said:
They taught this only with a vessel,
but with produce, no.
רב ששת said: Even with produce.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Argues about how far the ברייתא's rule reaches.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב נחמן: only a vessel works for חליפין. רב ששת: produce works too.

steps.title: What is רב נחמן's reason?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source of רב נחמן's limit.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason of רב נחמן?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רב נחמן excludes produce, setting up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן's limit needs a source, since the plain ברייתא could be read more broadly, as רב ששת does.

phrases.english: What is the reason of רב נחמן?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of רב נחמן's opinion.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source for limiting חליפין to vessels.

steps.title: The verse says 'his shoe': only a shoe-like item works
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן learns from the word 'his shoe' in the verse that only a shoe, meaning a vessel, works for חליפין, and not other things.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says 'his shoe.' A shoe, yes. Something else, no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives רב נחמן's source: the verse in רות speaks specifically of a shoe.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the verse names a shoe, which is a vessel-type item, רב נחמן limits חליפין to vessels like it. Produce is not like a shoe, so it does not work.
steps.whatToRemember: For רב נחמן, the 'shoe' in רות stands for a vessel, so only vessels work for חליפין. רב ששת allows even produce.

phrases.english: The verse says "his shoe":
phrases.notes: This is the word from רות 4:7, quoted earlier.

phrases.english: a shoe, yes;
something else, no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 23.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The verse names a shoe, so only a shoe-like item (a vessel) works, and not produce.

steps.title: What is רב ששת's source?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where רב ששת learns that produce can be used for חליפין.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason of רב ששת?
steps.whatsHappening: We just saw רב נחמן's source. Now the גמרא asks for the source of the other side, רב ששת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן limited חליפין to vessels because the פסוק says 'his shoe'. רב ששת allows even produce, so he needs his own reading of the same פסוק.

phrases.english: What is the reason of רב ששת?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Parallel to step 23, which asked for רב נחמן's source. Now the same question is asked about רב ששת.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The verse source for רב ששת's ruling that produce works for חליפין.

steps.title: רב ששת learns from 'to confirm all matters'
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת learns from 'לקיים כל דבר' that any item, even produce, can be used for חליפין.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'To confirm all matters.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers: רב ששת reads the words 'כל דבר', meaning 'every thing', as broad. So any item can be used to make the קנין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides use the same פסוק in רות. רב נחמן focuses on 'his shoe', while רב ששת focuses on 'all matters'. The question now becomes how each one handles the other's words.

phrases.english: The verse says: 'To confirm all matters.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 25.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'כל דבר' teaches that any item, including produce, can be used for חליפין.

steps.title: What does רב נחמן do with 'all matters'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב נחמן: the פסוק also says 'all matters', which sounds broad.
steps.simpleTranslation: For רב נחמן too, isn't it written 'to confirm all matters'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב נחמן. The words 'all matters' are in the פסוק, so how can he limit חליפין to vessels?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן cannot simply ignore part of the פסוק. He has to explain what 'כל דבר' teaches if it does not include produce.

phrases.english: According to רב נחמן too,
isn't it written: 'To confirm all matters'?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns רב ששת's verse against רב נחמן.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's limit of חליפין to vessels only.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק says 'all matters', which seems to include everything, even produce.

steps.title: 'All matters' means everything that can be acquired
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן explains that 'all matters' refers to the items being acquired through the shoe, not to what is used to make the קנין.
steps.simpleTranslation: That phrase, 'to confirm all matters', means all things that can be acquired by means of a shoe.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers for רב נחמן. 'All matters' describes what you can BUY with a shoe, meaning any item. It does not describe what you can use instead of the shoe.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two sides to a חליפין deal: the item handed over (the shoe) and the item being acquired. רב נחמן puts 'כל דבר' on the item being acquired. That leaves 'his shoe' to limit the item handed over to vessels.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the item USED for the קנין (the shoe) with the item being ACQUIRED. רב נחמן says 'all matters' is about the second one.

phrases.english: That 'to confirm all matters' means
all things that are acquired by means of a shoe.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends רב נחמן against step 27.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reassigning the verse's phrase to a different part of the transaction.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'All matters' seemed to describe what can be used for חליפין.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'All matters' describes what can be acquired, so only a vessel can be used.

steps.title: What does רב ששת do with 'his shoe'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב ששת: the פסוק says 'his shoe', which seems to limit חליפין to vessels.
steps.simpleTranslation: And for רב ששת too, isn't it written 'his shoe'?
steps.whatsHappening: Now the גמרא turns the question around. If רב ששת allows produce, what does he learn from the word 'his shoe'?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just as רב נחמן had to explain 'all matters', רב ששת has to explain 'his shoe'. The word seems to point to a specific kind of object.

phrases.english: And for רב ששת too,
isn't it written: 'his shoe'?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The mirror image of step 27: רב נחמן's verse is now used against רב ששת.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב ששת's ruling that produce works for חליפין.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'His shoe' seems to require a vessel, like a shoe.

steps.title: 'His shoe' teaches a complete item
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת learns from 'his shoe' only that the item must be whole, so half a pomegranate or half a nut cannot be used.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת would tell you: just as his shoe is a complete item, so too any complete item works. This excludes half a pomegranate and half a nut, which do not work.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers for רב ששת. 'His shoe' does not mean it must be a vessel. It means the item must be complete, the way a shoe is a complete thing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב ששת still learns something from 'נעלו', but only the quality of being whole. So a whole pomegranate works, but half of one does not.
steps.whatToRemember: רב נחמן: only vessels work for חליפין, and 'all matters' refers to what is acquired. רב ששת: any complete item works, even produce, and 'his shoe' teaches that it must be whole.

phrases.english: רב ששת would say to you:
Just as his shoe is a complete item,
so too any complete item works,

phrases.aramaic: לְאַפּוֹקֵי חֲצִי רִמּוֹן וַחֲצִי אֱגוֹז, דְּלָא.
phrases.english: to exclude half a pomegranate and half a nut, which do not work.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends רב ששת against step 29.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing what the verse's word teaches.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'His shoe' seemed to require a vessel.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'His shoe' only requires a complete item, so produce works if it is whole.

steps.title: Whose view does the document wording follow?
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת בריה דרב אידי asks whose opinion is followed by the standard document phrase 'with a vessel that is fit to acquire with it'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת the son of רב אידי said: Whose view do we follow when we write nowadays 'with a vessel that is fit to acquire with it'?
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic opens: the wording that scribes put into documents. The question sets up the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every word in a legal document is chosen on purpose. He is about to show that each word rules out a specific opinion.
steps.confusionAlert: רב ששת בריה דרב אידי is a different person from the רב ששת in the argument above. In fact, his explanation rules against that רב ששת.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִידִי:
phrases.english: רב ששת, the son of רב אידי, said:
According to whom do we write nowadays
'with a vessel that is fit to acquire with it'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the verse derivations to how the law is applied in document wording.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which opinions the standard קנין wording follows or rules out.

steps.title: Each word of the formula excludes an opinion
steps.stepSummary: 'With a vessel' excludes רב ששת, who allows produce. 'That is fit' excludes שמואל, whose view continues on the next page.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'With a vessel' excludes רב ששת, who says one acquires with produce. 'That is fit' excludes שמואל, who says one acquires...
steps.whatsHappening: He explains the formula word by word. Each word is there to rule out a different opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Writing 'with a vessel' shows that the practice follows רב נחמן, not רב ששת. The word 'fit' rejects a view of שמואל, and the sentence finishes on the next page.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows the practical הלכה. Since the documents say 'with a vessel', the practice follows רב נחמן that produce cannot be used for חליפין.

phrases.english: 'With a vessel' comes to exclude the view of רב ששת,
who says one may acquire with produce.
'That is fit' comes to exclude the view of שמואל,
who says one may acquire...

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 31.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'With a vessel' rejects רב ששת, and 'that is fit' rejects שמואל.
